reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all 6 files and found them safe, including LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml which Report 1 failed to review due to API errors. Report 1's inconclusive verdict was caused by tool failures (HTTP 400 errors), not security concerns. The files Report 1 could review were all found safe. disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors in Report 1, not actual security concerns. Report 1 encountered HTTP 400 BadRequestError when trying to audit LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml, forcing an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 successfully reviewed these same files and found them safe. coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to review LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in verdict determination - an inconclusive due to tool failure should not block a safe verdict when another report provides complete coverage
When multiple reports exist, prioritize the one with complete file coverage over one with tool errors, even if the complete report comes from a smaller/cheaper model
API error handling should allow retry logic or fallback to prevent single file failures from cascading into package-level inconclusive verdicts
